decisions.question: What should change?
decisions.chosen: Clear the 14 pre-existing design_check findings in index.html: remove the .card:before stripe; restyle kbd's 2px bottom border as an inset box-shadow; make the .disc disclaimer 12px in #75624e (5.03:1 on #f6eedd)
decisions.rationale: design_check exits 2 on main, so every UI checkpoint's design gate fails. impeccable can only waive these rules file-wide ('*'), which would also hide future real findings, so fix rather than waive. User chose remove-stripe and restyle-keycap.

decisions.question: How do we know it is done?
decisions.chosen: npx --yes impeccable@4 detect --quiet client index.html exits 0 with no ignores config and no inline waivers; npm test passes, including a test that the disclaimer is >=12px and >=4.5:1 contrast against --paper
decisions.rationale: The detector is the gate's own check; the unit test guards the one real accessibility defect in the offline test suite.

decisions.question: What should change?
decisions.chosen: Move the game from pincode-generated fictional towns to three real AP towns (Pulivendula and Kadapa in Kadapa district, Punganur in Chittoor district) and retell Nomination Day as YSRCP candidates being obstructed by a TDP mob backed by police: stone pelting, arson of YSRCP supporters' houses and vehicles, and a post-filing scrutiny where only 4 of 10 filed nominations survive.
decisions.rationale: User's spec message; plan approved in plan mode.

decisions.question: What is in and out?
decisions.chosen: IN: 3 real towns from OSM; pincode lookup removed; YSRCP hero party with blue three-blade-fan flag; TDP rival with yellow flag; stone-throwing TDP mobs; police that escort mobs and never arrest them; arson of supporters' houses and vehicles; per-town invented YSRCP ally and TDP leader; scrutiny ending 10 filed / 6 torn / 4 accepted. OUT: any real person as a character (named leaders, DGP, real officers), the quoted threat lines, the name 'Babu' for Punganur's leader, online multiplayer, new modes. Polling Day mode stays, with the new towns and mob.
decisions.rationale: Agreed in plan mode, including the content line the user accepted.

decisions.question: Content and technical constraints?
decisions.chosen: Content: real parties (YSRCP, TDP) named; every person invented; all dialogue original; disclaimer 'Satire. All characters and the events shown are fictional; no real person is depicted. Map data (c) OpenStreetMap contributors.' Technical: no build step, no runtime dependencies, deterministic sim (no Math.random), shared UMD modules run in browser and Node, design_check must stay at 0 findings.
decisions.rationale: Plan approval; existing architecture in README.

decisions.question: Where does town data come from?
decisions.chosen: Overpass API, fetched once by scripts/fetch-osm.js into data/towns/<id>.json (projected to metres, trimmed to roads, buildings, water, landmarks, neighbourhood names) and committed; ODbL attribution in menu and README, data/towns/README.md.
decisions.rationale: User chose 'Allow overpass-api.de' over a local script or runtime fetch.

decisions.question: Which external services does the game call?
decisions.chosen: None at runtime: the India Post pincode lookup is removed with client/pincode.js. Overpass is called only by the hand-run fetch script.
decisions.rationale: User chose 'Only the 3 towns'; baked data keeps the game offline and tests deterministic.

decisions.question: How will the user judge done?
decisions.chosen: Each town loads with its real street layout; TDP mobs throw stones and police escort them; supporters' houses and vehicles burn and block streets; the ally joins; after filing, the scrutiny panel shows 10 filed, 6 torn, 4 accepted; npm test green incl. bot completing both modes in all three towns; design_check 0 findings.

decisions.question: Who plays it?
decisions.recommended: Telugu-speaking players in Andhra Pradesh, mostly YSRCP sympathisers sharing it on WhatsApp and social media; casual gamers.

decisions.question: Which persona matters first?
decisions.recommended: Mobile-first casual player on a mid-range Android phone with touch controls; desktop keyboard players second.

decisions.question: Critical flows, ranked?
decisions.recommended: 1) Pick town and Nomination Day, play to filing, see the scrutiny panel. 2) Same for Polling Day. 3) Leaderboard per town.

decisions.question: Stack?
decisions.recommended: Unchanged: plain JS UMD modules, Canvas 2D, Node 18 node:test, no bundler or runtime deps; the fetch script uses Node's built-in fetch.

decisions.question: Performance, size, offline?
decisions.recommended: Smooth on a mid-range phone with up to ~40 extra entities (mob, stones, fires); each data/towns JSON <= 400 KB; works offline after load; replays stay deterministic.

decisions.question: What does success look like?
decisions.recommended: All three towns playable start to finish (bot test green on each, both modes) and the user accepts the look of towns, mob, fires and scrutiny panel at review.

decisions.question: Visual direction?
decisions.recommended: Keep the existing visual system (paper-card menu, top-down canvas sprites, blue #1e5bd8); add TDP yellow #f2c200, flames and smoke, and a torn-paper scrutiny panel in the same card style; keep design_check at 0.

decisions.question: Accessibility target?
decisions.recommended: WCAG 2.2 AA for menu and panels (contrast, >=12px text, keyboard-operable town picker, visible focus); existing keyboard controls in play; respect prefers-reduced-motion for the scrutiny animation.

decisions.question: Build order while overpass-api.de is blocked here?
decisions.recommended: Non-OSM features first on the current generated maps keyed by town id (towns/parties/picker, TDP mob, arson, characters, scrutiny), then the OSM builder with Pulivendula, then Kadapa and Punganur.

decisions.question: How are e2e, a11y and responsive checks run?
decisions.recommended: Add playwright-core as the only devDependency (no browser download; uses /opt/pw-browsers/chromium) with a separate 'npm run e2e' wired to forge's e2e command; 'npm test' stays dependency-free.
